text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. Developers often refactor to make their code easier to read and understand. This is important because clean code is simpler to maintain and update. Over time, software can build up technical debt, which means problems pile up when quick fixes are used instead of proper solutions. Refactoring helps reduce this debt by cleaning up messy parts of the code. A good rule is that after refactoring, the program should behave exactly the same as before. Teams usually test their code carefully to make sure nothing breaks during the process.
